I toss aside a utensil and pick up another. Shure: "Hmm, upstairs." "Very Chinese, very Chinese," I say. "Let's not make spaghetti," I add, laughing. Tasha: "Was this activity originally planned?" I turn my head and keep washing the dishes, saying, "I'll keep washing the dishes." "Yes, there was a cooking activity, but no spaghetti-making activity," I say. Alice: \u4f60\u4eec\u559c\u6b22\u9178\u6c64\u5a03\u5a03\u83dc\u5417 Alice: "I really like drinking that flavorful one." "We can make one," I say. I watch everyone talk as I turn and wash the dishes. Alice: "Okay, do you eat mushrooms?" Tasha: "Sure." Alice: "Do you eat century eggs?"

[DAY1 14:00:30 - DAY1 14:01:00]
I wash the dishes, looking left and right as I work. "They're preserved eggs," Alice says. "The black ones," Alice adds. Tasha says, "Never had them either." "That's good," I say. Tasha says, "They look really ugly." "Yes, yes. Even if you don't want to, give it a try," I say. I turn my head left and speak. Tasha says, "I really don't want to eat it." I watch everyone talk. "You can give it a try, right?" I ask. Tasha says, "This is really ugly." Lucia says, "I thought century eggs were a regional dish." I sit down, lower my head, and speak. Lucia says, "Like maybe from your area." I put down my utensils. Alice says, "It's a cold dish." I turn my head to the right and pick up new utensils. Lucia says, "But I also eat it well." Alice says, "You just don't eat it on your own." I turn on the faucet and wash the dishes. Alice says, "Oh, right." I continue washing the dishes. Alice says, "Not sure if it's enough." I turn off the faucet and keep washing, then rinse and clean the dishes. Alice says, "Let's buy a few." Alice says, "Let me write it down."

I initiated the shelving installation by opening a box and assembling rods and poles onto the shelf frame, coordinating with Shure to use a lever and turntable for precise placement. I supported and adjusted the frame, moving around the structure to ensure proper alignment. Throughout this process, I engaged in detailed discussions with Tasha, Lucia, Alice, and Shure, examining boxes and edges, considering measurements, and collaboratively refining the installation plan to resolve fitting issues. This established the foundational structure for the shelving setup.

As assembly continued, I actively manipulated parts by rotating boxes, supporting racks, and operating joysticks alongside Shure to adjust the shelf height. I handed repaired components to Shure and assisted in installing the whiteboard onto the rack by carefully holding and positioning it under Lucia’s direction. The team analyzed the whiteboard sections' edges and connections, debating necessary adjustments and repositioning segments through trial and error to achieve accurate assembly. I maintained focus on structural stability and confirmed placements with the group, resulting in a securely installed shelving unit and whiteboard.

During a break, I briefly conversed with Shure and Katrina about tiredness and sleep schedules, suggesting we get two cups of coffee from a manual coffee machine upstairs. Preparing to leave the area, I moved a stool and headed toward the stairs while Katrina mentioned pending vase deliveries and planned golf cart rides. Concurrently, I used my phone to gather information about venue conditions, learning from Katrina that the upstairs area was hotter with poor ventilation and limited airflow improvement. We also discussed the expected arrival of a short-haired person required at the lab by noon, confirming their logistics and clock-in requirements.

I proposed setting up the larger second floor as the event venue, suggesting relocating chairs and sofas upstairs to improve movement and space utilization. Shure and Katrina confirmed the plan to host product introductions and self-introductions there. Alice and Lucia compared the second floor with other available locations, while Tasha observed my physical strain during the discussion. Additionally, Shure inquired about the coffee location and a fridge unplugging incident; I confirmed that no one had touched the fridge, concluding the issue remained unresolved but acknowledged.

After completion, I engaged in conversations regarding the puzzle’s design symbolism and shared observations with Alice and Lucia while maintaining active physical interaction with the puzzle throughout.

I facilitated the transition to reviewing Tasha’s baking tools by handling items such as molds, whisks, and piping tips and discussing their functions and prices. I coordinated coffee preparation despite limited supplies and assisted in appliance arrangement by moving the oven and microwave. I oversaw ingredient organization and placed a takeout food order via phone, confirming meal selections with Shure to align delivery timing with task completion, concluding the coordinated setup and meal planning phase.

I initiated a group discussion about available food items and their storage, with Tasha confirming placements like bread and a battery on the table. The group agreed to refrigerate chocolate to prevent melting, establishing clarity on existing food and storage arrangements. Subsequently, I took charge of ordering food using my phone, confirming meal sets and dish preferences with Tasha and others. I coordinated with Alice and Lucia to finalize the order, deciding on three meals without drinks and incorporating group input. The orders were placed after group confirmation, concluding the food procurement phase.

Simultaneously, discussions on storing perishables continued among Tasha, Alice, and Lucia, who arranged chocolates in the fridge and assessed space availability. I remained engaged by sharing my phone screen to review meal options and confirmed preferences such as excluding drinks for Alice. The group agreed to rearrange fridge items for efficient space use. I invited Lucia to review the orders on my phone, prompting her evaluation of the selected items. Shure questioned changes to the order, specifically about additions and removals. Lucia expressed hesitation over a durian cheese item, which I acknowledged without further action, closing the group’s review and contemplation of food choices.

Moving through the space, I showed Lucia my phone and assisted her with it while joining conversations about vodka flavors and organizing the area into personality-based zones designated as “J zones” and “P zones.” I participated by asking clarifying questions and commenting on clutter, supporting collaborative spatial organization. I inquired about drying the powder, which was approved, and coordinated placement of items following Alice’s directions to avoid blocking spaces. I also moved a shelf and contributed to organizing the area, maintaining group engagement.

I consulted with Shure and others to finalize supply orders, adjusting quantities based on available utensils. The group discussed drink options, agreeing on a cocktail plan and scheduling two supply rounds, with Shure planning a dorm check the next day. I managed kitchenware cleaning instructions from Tasha and performed dishwashing tasks, coordinating with Lucia and Tasha on drink preparations and cleaning protocols.

Throughout cleaning tasks, I washed trays, utensils, and pots under running water, managing kitchenware systematically. Discussions among the group covered beverage supplies and potential cocktail ingredients. I researched recipes and confirmed cleaning arrangements. I proposed a puzzle activity to encourage breaks and group collaboration, supported organizational plans for kitchenware and supplies, and monitored time to ensure task completion.

I actively participated in discussions about kitchen supplies, shopping lists, and ingredient needs while washing dishes. The group decided which boxes to keep or discard for storage purposes and coordinated coffee-related preparations while planning for restocking supplies. I cleaned cooking utensils thoroughly, including pots and cutting boards, while engaging the group in conversations about personality types and event participation. I confirmed disposal of unnecessary adapters and contributed to meal planning discussions, maintaining progress on cleaning and organization.

During cooking-related activities, I washed dishes and moved between tasks like mopping and waste disposal. I engaged in meal planning with the group, discussing dish preferences and kitchen tool usage, ensuring combined efforts in cooking preparation and kitchen maintenance. I continued washing dishes attentively, monitoring water temperature with the group and addressing questions about missing items such as a battery bag. Ownership of personal belongings was clarified, and equipment functionality was confirmed, supporting a systematic cleaning process.

While washing dishes, I engaged in casual conversations about sleep habits, clock purchases, and meal timing. I briefly wrote on the whiteboard and resumed cleaning, contributing to group decisions on item retention and environmental practices aimed at reducing clutter and waste. I handled a kitchen rack used for roasting, confirming its operation and cleaning it thoroughly. Afterward, I retrieved a box and answered a phone call regarding a delivery, marking a transition from cleaning tasks to communication.

Exiting the building, I turned off my phone and walked to a restaurant to collect KFC takeout. I thanked the staff and returned inside the building. I discussed dining options with the group and confirmed plans to eat outside. Upon exiting to the yard, I opened an umbrella and set the takeout on an outdoor table. I noted a powerless device, prompting a technical check involving Shure and Katrina. I verified phone recording statuses and screen displays alongside Katrina. The group discussed dining area cleanliness and agreed on using disposable tablecloths despite conceptual conflicts. Technical issues related to a drained power bank were acknowledged, concluding the coordination for the outdoor dining setup.

Tasha says, "Got the strawberries, got the cream, mint and cling film. Didn't get the egg tarts." Tasha adds, "I'm already getting thirsty."

"No MSG, okay," I say while holding the shopping cart with one hand and looking toward Alice. Tasha says, "MSG and chicken essence are similar." I take two steps. Alice says, "MSG is a bit healthier." Tasha says, "Remove the chicken essence." Alice says, "Chicken essence has more additives." I watch Tasha take the product from Alice and put it in the car. "Oh, it's fine," I say. "We've lived this long," I add.

[DAY1 17:38:01 - DAY1 17:38:29]
Alice: "Yeah, have you tried locust flower? You can stir-fry it or make buns with it." Tasha: "No." I walk over. Alice: "It's really tasty, sweet." "What do you mean?" I ask. "I'll look into it," I say. I raise my right hand and pick up a vegetable, picking up fragments and placing them in my palm. Tasha: "Did you buy enoki mushrooms?" Alice: "Got them, got them." "Why did it spill?" I ask. Alice: "It fell through the crack." Tasha: "Then eat it quickly, don't waste it." I sniff it repeatedly. Alice: "No, you can't eat it raw." "Haha, poisoning," I say. Alice: "It's fine, don't tell him. Let him eat it." I weigh the vegetable pieces. "What will happen if he eats it?" I ask. Alice: "It won't taste good." "The main thing is it won't taste good, right?" I say. Katrina: "Is lime better or lemon better?" Tasha: "Seasonings, we have pepper, MSG, and salt." Alice: "Salt." Shure: "Get them all."

[DAY1 17:33:02 - DAY1 17:33:29]
Tasha walks to the merchandise on my front-left and stops. I say, "I'll come along too." Tasha: "Buy eggs and get century eggs for free." We're choosing together. Tasha: "Perfect." I say, "Perfect timing." Alice: "Fresh eggs?" Tasha: "Yeah, fresh eggs are fine too." I raise my hand and point at the product in front and ask, "Is your home far from Gaoyou?" Tasha turns to me. Alice: "Gaoyou salted duck eggs." Tasha: "Not far." Alice: "Salted duck eggs." Tasha: "Your home isn't far either." I say, "Yeah, that's true."

[DAY1 17:33:30 - DAY1 17:34:00]
I watch Tasha pick up a box of goods. Alice: "Oh, that one can be eaten raw." Tasha: "I think it's enough to buy a little of the edible one, and we can buy a box of this too." Alice: "Sure." Tasha: "Let's buy this—uh, to make tiramisu." Alice: "For the tiramisu?" Tasha: "Yes, everything else can be used. Use non-sterilized eggs." Alice: "Cooked ones are fine." "Okay," I say. "What's a sterilized egg?" I ask. Tasha: "A sterilized egg is one you can eat right away — it probably doesn't have bacteria." "Why is it called a sterilized egg?" I ask.

Holding my phone, I adjusted its screen for clarity and passed it to Alice for verification. This concluded our technical verification and transitioned us into a casual group discussion about feeding AI content from TikTok, prompted by Shure’s suggestion, with brief comments on content creator Chen Ze, establishing a relaxed atmosphere before proceeding.

Shure obtained directions to Hema Fresh from a passerby, confirming pedestrians must take a longer route. We decided to proceed along the roadside under Shure and Katrina’s guidance, noting a person with long legs had already crossed ahead. While walking, I checked my phone, adjusted my equipment, and inquired about giving a helmet to a runner. Lucia declined to follow due to her outfit, and we acknowledged the main gate lacked access control as we moved toward our destination, maintaining group coordination during navigation.

Approaching the supermarket, I encountered Tasha coming from the left and joined the group, initiating conversation about a broken item that had fallen off. I commented on a singing quality before we entered a large Beijing supermarket. Inside, I checked my phone while walking. Noticing others had already ascended upstairs quickly, I responded to Tasha’s question about their pace. I saw Katrina, Shure, and Lucia enter through the front door and followed them onto the escalator, during which Katrina and Shure explained their delay due to shoelaces and following the guide. I showed Katrina a card from my backpack explaining its effect in sunlight, receiving a positive response, consolidating our group’s awareness and readiness.

I proceeded to the blue promotional area at the supermarket’s front right, inquiring about its location. Alice identified an item described as big eyes with long eyelashes, eliciting group reactions and an apology from Lucia. Alice invited AI to join, and Katrina mentioned the nearby HLA store, which Shure identified as a men’s wardrobe brand. I questioned the store’s visibility and inquired about a toxic smell in the area. Tasha provided me glasses to test the environment, while Lucia commented on recent renovations. I examined pictures on a blue easel wall searching for the HLA logo; Tasha and Alice provided related observations. I asked about HLA and its logo, and Lucia explained it was a men’s clothing brand. Alice suggested AI could locate it, and the group discussed logo similarities, without reaching definitive conclusions, reflecting our investigative approach to store identification.

I approached two shopping carts and selected one. We discussed logistics for purchasing alcohol and groceries, deciding alcohol should have its own smaller cart. Lucia confirmed the smaller cart was child-sized; I noted children likely do not fit comfortably, jokingly suggesting they might be for cats. Tasha, Alice, and Lucia engaged in this exchange. Alice pushed the cart while Lucia placed her hand on it as we moved through the area, establishing our approach to organized shopping.

At the Hema Fresh supermarket entrance, I pointed out products as we entered. The group commented on pricing; Alice questioned durian’s low price, and Tasha mentioned a promotional offer. We turned left and discussed whether to split up or stay together; Shure asked for a decision, and I considered options while planning next steps, marking our transition into active engagement in supermarket shopping.

Inside the supermarket, I inquired about assigned tasks and routes. Tasha, Alice, and I discussed walking once around with augmented reality glasses reconstructing the mall in 3D. Tasha and Katrina used their phones to arrange group divisions for shopping, with Katrina proposing splits by product types and floors. The plan was finalized for shopping and task distribution, ensuring efficient coverage.

The group planned purchasing alcohol and drink ingredients. Katrina initiated alcohol selection; Tasha, Lucia, and I acknowledged having some drink knowledge, though I admitted my lack of expertise while browsing. Katrina expressed interest in rum and green Shine Muscat grapes, supported by Lucia and Tasha. We proceeded toward the beverage section, aligning our shopping objectives.

At the beverage area, Tasha and Alice compared strawberry boxes for quantity and quality. I assisted by holding products and pushing the cart. After evaluation, Tasha selected the larger box, confirmed by Alice to weigh about 500 grams. The group finalized the choice and added it to the cart, completing the fruit selection stage.

While shopping, I pushed the cart and reviewed prices. Tasha advised against eating freshly cut fruit, suggesting only good parts be sold separately. I proposed educating consumers by selling good and bad parts separately. Tasha checked further details on her phone, indicating ongoing planning, reflecting our attention to consumer guidance.

I pushed the cart through the fruit section with Alice, discussing blueberries and pineapples. Tasha added a box to the cart. I inspected a pineapple package and accidentally pricked my hand. We considered adding a yellow mango based on Alice’s suggestion; Tasha agreed. I pointed at the pineapple while Alice and Tasha discussed dessert fruit options, then walked to the counter where we debated buying fresh-cut pineapple or having staff cut it. Tasha recommended staff cutting, which I agreed to, finalizing preparation for dessert fruit.

We decided not to include pineapple in dessert but to eat it ourselves. I requested staff cut the pineapple and captured a close-up of the cutting process while Tasha explained assistance options. I compared pineapples with Alice to determine ripeness, selecting one together. We approached the sales assistant, requested cutting, and I briefly conversed about timing and process, confirming readiness.

Tasha pointed out mini Thai mangoes as the sweetest option and instructed me to select a box, noting mold on one. I chose another box after her guidance. Alice and Tasha confirmed sweetness and softness, and I verified quantity before Tasha finalized the selection. The group agreed and completed fruit selection, consolidating our dessert ingredient list.

I navigated with the cart while Tasha directed me to locate pasteurized egg milk. We confirmed fruit items and focused on milk products; Tasha added two milk boxes to the cart. We compared coconut water prices and sizes, reviewing inventory and confirming milk quantity sufficiency, progressing toward dairy procurement.

I inquired about heavy cream location; Alice and Tasha suggested the freezer near yogurt. I asked staff about heavy cream availability, then joined Katrina and Shure, discussing coconut water and milk while managing the cart and monitoring purchases, maintaining group coordination.

I assessed shopping progress reviewing Tasha and Alice’s choices, noting pace. The group debated coconut milk versus water preferences. I moved around facilitating decisions and verifying essential product locations, including whipping cream, ensuring completeness.

I assisted Tasha and Alice selecting product styles during discussion of Anchor and Nestlé brands and prices. Spotting Katrina and Shure approaching, I asked a salesperson about whipping cream location and quantity, noting insufficiency. After Tasha checked delivery options, I suggested choosing a product and discussed placing online orders if in-store supply was inadequate, establishing need for additional orders and delivery timing, ensuring procurement continuity.

Browsing with Tasha, Alice, and Lucia, I accepted drinks from Tasha and offered to carry them, briefly discussing product cuteness and quantity. The group planned baking a cake on the 22nd, considering online orders for ingredients. I proposed ordering online to ensure availability; the team reviewed the shopping list including sterilized eggs and baking essentials, consolidating ingredient procurement and baking preparation.

As we moved, Tasha listed required items on her phone: eggs, sugar, salt, milk powder, coffee, whipped cream, mint, cling film, tart crusts, strawberries, enoki mushrooms, century eggs, and baby bok choy. I confirmed the list and directed the group to pick up baby bok choy, finalizing the shopping plan and aligning on baking ingredients, solidifying our coordinated approach.

I walked with Tasha selecting eggs, during which Tasha mentioned a promotion offering free century eggs with fresh egg purchase. I confirmed selection while Alice questioned freshness; Tasha confirmed eggs were fresh. We discussed proximity of homes to Gaoyou and specific egg varieties like Gaoyou salted duck eggs. I continued choosing items for Tiramisu; Alice noted some eggs could be eaten raw, and Tasha suggested buying small amounts of those with non-sterilized eggs for the recipe, clarifying sterilized eggs as safe to eat immediately due to absence of bacteria, ensuring informed selection.

Proceeding to the freezer section, Tasha listed needed ingredients including sterilized eggs, milk, sugar, and salt. Alice pointed out seasoning and vegetable locations, suggesting mushroom purchase. I encouraged this; a price discussion arose about napa cabbage, which I explained was expensive due to mountain freshness. Alice questioned availability of regular cabbage; I replied no. Tasha asked about my food preferences; Alice confirmed napa cabbage identity, maintaining awareness of produce quality and pricing.

Continuing to select vegetables, Alice picked a box while discussing cost. When asked about buying napa cabbage, Alice declined due to price. Tasha proposed sourcing vegetables from her garden or buying Shanghai Bok Choy as cheaper alternative, though Alice noted it lacked desired flavor. I pushed the cart forward while Alice and I discussed cabbage price differences and cost per kilogram, with Alice confirming the high price, reflecting cost considerations.

I examined a drink bottle while Tasha and Alice discussed its price and type; Alice confirmed vegetable prices and recommended a purchase. Katrina, Shure, and Lucia joined; we discussed previous purchases like sterilized eggs and hot pot soup bases and questioned peach juice availability, which I noted seemed assigned to us, consolidating inventory awareness.

We discussed an unusual task involving masking tape; Katrina explained its use and suggested online purchase. Alice agreed to buy more; Tasha proposed checking a stationery store, and Katrina reminded us about pending ice cube mold purchase. Walking with Lucia and Katrina, we debated Hema’s main purpose and considered buying napa cabbage, aligning shopping priorities.

I checked the freezer, conversing with Tasha and Alice about spring vegetables and locust flower. I picked up and weighed vegetable fragments while Alice described locust flower cooking methods. I inquired about an item spill, learning it fell through a crack; the group discussed whether it could be eaten raw, concluding it would not taste good and warning against waste, ensuring food safety.

Continuing to pick vegetables with Alice and Tasha, I confirmed familiarity with locust flower and asked about scallions
